# Package Requirements
```{r}
if (!base::requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) utils::install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("limma")
BiocManager::install("mixOmics")
```

# Generate Example Dataset
```{r}
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Example Dataset Generation — More Realistic Expression Values
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Creates:
#   • cell_signals.csv — 40 samples × 60 features (approx. log2 intensities)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

base::set.seed(42)
n_samp <- 40L
n_feat <- 60L
grp <- base::factor(rep(c("control","treated"), each = n_samp/2L))

# Latent biological components (e.g., pathway activity, batch, noise)
latent_signal <- stats::rnorm(n_samp, mean = ifelse(grp == "treated", 1.0, 0.0), sd = 0.8)
latent_batch  <- stats::rnorm(n_samp, mean = 0.0, sd = 1.0)

# Feature-specific baselines and sensitivities
baseline <- stats::rnorm(n_feat, mean = 8.0, sd = 0.7)   # typical log2 range
sens1    <- stats::rnorm(n_feat, mean = 0.8, sd = 0.3)   # treatment effect strength
sens2    <- stats::rnorm(n_feat, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.3)   # batch effect strength

# Generate matrix on log2 scale
X <- base::outer(latent_signal, sens1) + base::outer(latent_batch, sens2) +
     base::matrix(stats::rnorm(n_samp * n_feat, 0, 0.4), n_samp, n_feat) +
     base::rep(baseline, each = n_samp)

# Back-transform to intensity scale to mimic expression counts
expr_values <- 2^X

cell_signals <- base::as.data.frame(expr_values)
base::colnames(cell_signals) <- paste0("Feat_", seq_len(n_feat))
cell_signals$Group <- grp
utils::write.csv(cell_signals, "cell_signals.csv", row.names = FALSE)
base::message("✅ Wrote cell_signals.csv (simulated expression-like data)")
```

# Task 1: Data Normalization
```{r}
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Task 1 — Data Normalization and log2 Transformation
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Load the provided dataset `cell_signals.csv`
# 2. Compute Z-scores feature-wise
# 3. Apply log2(x + 1) transformation. Why add 1?
# 4. Visualize distributions for one feature
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

cell_signals <- utils::read.csv("cell_signals.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
groups <- base::factor(cell_signals$Group)
Xnum <- base::as.matrix(cell_signals[, base::setdiff(colnames(cell_signals), "Group")])

X_z    <- base::scale(Xnum)           # Z-score normalization
X_log2 <- base::log2(Xnum + 1)        # Log2 transformation

# Histograms
graphics::par(mfrow = c(1,2))

graphics::hist(Xnum[,1],
               breaks = "FD", 
               main = "Raw Feat_1",
               xlab = "value",
               col = "grey20", border = "white")

br_z <- seq(-4, 4, by = 0.5)
graphics::hist(base::scale(Xnum[,1]),
               breaks = br_z,
               xlim = c(-4, 4),
               main = "Z Feat_1",
               xlab = "z",
               col = "grey20", border = "white")

graphics::par(mfrow = c(1,1))

# Density Plot
graphics::plot(stats::density(Xnum[,1]), main = "Raw vs log2 Feat_1", xlab = "", ylim = c(0, 0.5))
graphics::lines(stats::density(X_log2[,1]), col = 2)
graphics::legend("topright", legend = c("raw","log2"), lty = 1, col = c(1,2))
```

# Task 2: Complexity Reduction
```{r}
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Task 2 — PCA and PLS-DA (mixOmics::plotIndiv)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Run PCA on the z-scored matrix X_z
# 2. Visualize PC1–PC2 using mixOmics::plotIndiv
# 3. Run PLS-DA with labels in `groups`
# 4. Visualize comp1–comp2 using mixOmics::plotIndiv
# 5. Compare separations and interpret supervision effects
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# PCA
pca_res <- mixOmics::pca(X_z, ncomp = 3, center = FALSE, scale = FALSE)
mixOmics::plotIndiv(pca_res,
                    comp = c(1, 2),
                    group = groups,
                    ind.names = FALSE,
                    legend = TRUE,
                    title = "PCA — PC1 vs PC2")

# PLS-DA
plsda_res <- mixOmics::plsda(X_z, Y = groups, ncomp = 3)
mixOmics::plotIndiv(plsda_res,
                    comp = c(1, 2),
                    group = groups,
                    ind.names = FALSE,
                    legend = TRUE,
                    title = "PLS-DA — comp1 vs comp2")

# ── Most discriminative features for PLS-DA (by absolute loadings on comp1–2)
loadX <- plsda_res$loadings$X                      # variables × components
comp_use <- 1:2                                    # change if you want more comps
score_abs <- base::rowSums(base::abs(loadX[, comp_use, drop = FALSE]))
ord <- base::order(score_abs, decreasing = TRUE)

topN <- 15L
top_tbl <- base::data.frame(
  Feature       = base::rownames(loadX)[ord][seq_len(topN)],
  Loading_comp1 = loadX[ord, 1][seq_len(topN)],
  Loading_comp2 = loadX[ord, 2][seq_len(topN)],
  DiscrimScore  = score_abs[ord][seq_len(topN)],
  row.names     = NULL,
  check.names   = FALSE
)

# Print top discriminative hits by component difference
base::print(top_tbl)

# VIP scores, also report them
vip_mat <- mixOmics::vip(plsda_res)              # variables × components
vip_score <- base::rowMeans(vip_mat[, comp_use, drop = FALSE])
top_vip_ord <- base::order(vip_score, decreasing = TRUE)
top_vip <- base::data.frame(
  Feature  = base::rownames(vip_mat)[top_vip_ord][seq_len(topN)],
  VIP_mean = vip_score[top_vip_ord][seq_len(topN)],
  row.names = NULL
)

# Print top discriminative hits by VIP score
base::print(top_vip)
```

# Task 3: Clustering Algorithms
```{r}
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Task 3 — Clustering Algorithms
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Perform hierarchical clustering on X_z (z-scored cell_signals data)
# 2. Cut dendrogram into 3 clusters
# 3. Compare cluster assignment to group labels. Are there significant differences in sample distributions throughout the cluster? How to test this?
# 4. Perform k-means (k = 3) directly on X_z
# 5. Visualize k-means clusters using mixOmics::plotIndiv from a PCA object
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# 1) Hierarchical clustering based on sample distances
dist_mat <- stats::dist(X_z, method = "euclidean")
hc <- stats::hclust(dist_mat, method = "complete")

# Plot with group labels
graphics::plot(hc,
               labels = as.character(groups),
               main = "Hierarchical Clustering (complete linkage)",
               sub  = "Distance: Euclidean | Linkage: complete")

# Plot with sample names
sample_names <- base::rownames(X_z)
if (is.null(sample_names) || anyNA(sample_names) || any(sample_names == "")) {
  sample_names <- paste0("Sample_", sprintf("%02d", seq_len(nrow(X_z))))
}

graphics::plot(hc,
               labels = sample_names,
               main = "Hierarchical Clustering — sample names",
               sub  = "Distance: Euclidean | Linkage: complete",
               cex  = 0.8,            # shrink label text a bit
               hang = -0.1)           # pull leaves to a common baseline

# 2) Cut tree into 3 clusters
cl3 <- stats::cutree(hc, k = 3L)

# 3) Compare hierarchical clusters with biological groups
base::table(Hierarchical = cl3, Group = groups)

# 4) K-means directly on normalized cell signal matrix
set_k <- 3L
km <- stats::kmeans(X_z, centers = set_k, nstart = 25)
base::table(Kmeans = km$cluster, Group = groups)

# 5) PCA for visualization and plotting with mixOmics::plotIndiv
pca_res <- mixOmics::pca(X_z, ncomp = 2, center = FALSE, scale = FALSE)
mixOmics::plotIndiv(pca_res,
                    comp = c(1, 2),
                    group = base::factor(km$cluster),
                    ind.names = FALSE,
                    legend = TRUE,
                    title = "k-means clusters visualized in PCA space")
```

# Task 4: Linear Models for Microarrays
```{r}
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Task 4 — LIMMA differential expression (knockout vs wildtype)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Read expression data and sample information
# 2. Build design and contrast matrices
# 3. Fit linear models with empirical Bayes moderation
# 4. Adjust p-values (raw, BH, Bonferroni)
# 5. Create volcano plots and report significant counts
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# Load data
ge <- utils::read.csv("gene_expression_for_LIMMA.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
si <- utils::read.csv("sample_info.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Match samples across both files
common <- base::intersect(colnames(ge), si$Sample)
ge <- ge[, common, drop = FALSE]
si <- si[match(common, si$Sample), , drop = FALSE]

# Log2 transform
expr_log2 <- base::log2(ge + 1)

# Build design matrix
fac <- base::factor(si$Condition)
design <- stats::model.matrix(~ 0 + fac)
base::colnames(design) <- base::levels(fac)

# Ensure correct column names for contrast
base::message("Design matrix columns: ", paste(base::colnames(design), collapse = ", "))

# Contrast: knockout vs wildtype
contrast_mat <- limma::makeContrasts(knockout_vs_wildtype = knockout - wildtype, levels = design)

# Fit linear models
fit  <- limma::lmFit(expr_log2, design)
fit2 <- limma::contrasts.fit(fit, contrast_mat)
fit2 <- limma::eBayes(fit2)

# Extract results for all features
tab <- limma::topTable(fit2, number = base::nrow(expr_log2), sort.by = "P")

# Add p-value adjustments
tab$P_raw  <- tab$P.Value
tab$P_BH   <- stats::p.adjust(tab$P_raw, method = "BH")
tab$P_Bonf <- stats::p.adjust(tab$P_raw, method = "bonferroni")

# Significance flags
tab$Sig_raw  <- tab$P_raw  < 0.05
tab$Sig_BH   <- tab$P_BH   < 0.05
tab$Sig_Bonf <- tab$P_Bonf < 0.05

# ── Robust NA handling for counts and plots
n_raw  <- base::sum(tab$Sig_raw,  na.rm = TRUE)
n_bh   <- base::sum(tab$Sig_BH,   na.rm = TRUE)
n_bonf <- base::sum(tab$Sig_Bonf, na.rm = TRUE)

base::message(sprintf(
  "Significant genes @0.05 — raw=%d, BH=%d, Bonf=%d",
  n_raw, n_bh, n_bonf
))

# Drop NA rows for plotting
tab_plot <- tab[stats::complete.cases(tab[, c("logFC","P_raw","P_BH","P_Bonf")]), , drop = FALSE]

# ── Volcano plots
graphics::par(mfrow = c(1,3))

graphics::plot(tab_plot$logFC, -base::log10(tab_plot$P_raw),
               pch = 16, col = ifelse(tab_plot$P_raw < 0.05, 2, 1),
               xlab = "logFC (knockout – wildtype)",
               ylab = "-log10 p",
               main = "Volcano — Raw p")
graphics::abline(h = -base::log10(0.05), lty = 2)

graphics::plot(tab_plot$logFC, -base::log10(tab_plot$P_BH),
               pch = 16, col = ifelse(tab_plot$P_BH < 0.05, 2, 1),
               xlab = "logFC", ylab = "-log10 BH p",
               main = "Volcano — BH adjusted")
graphics::abline(h = -base::log10(0.05), lty = 2)

graphics::plot(tab_plot$logFC, -base::log10(tab_plot$P_Bonf),
               pch = 16, col = ifelse(tab_plot$P_Bonf < 0.05, 2, 1),
               xlab = "logFC", ylab = "-log10 Bonf p",
               main = "Volcano — Bonferroni adjusted")
graphics::abline(h = -base::log10(0.05), lty = 2)

graphics::par(mfrow = c(1,1))

```
